note: Configuration for the deterministic recommendation wizard (recommend_engine.php). Weights are editorial choices published on the page ('How we matched'). Only capabilities that sourced profiles document can add points; unknown capabilities never add or subtract points. Add an objective only when at least two reviewed tools document its primary capability (a test enforces this).

write_content.label: Write and edit (emails, documents, copy)
workflow: Collect 2 or 3 real pieces of writing you need to produce this week (an email, a short report, a page of copy).
Write a one-paragraph brief for each: audience, goal, tone and length.
Generate a first draft with {t1}, then edit it yourself. Keep notes on what you had to fix.
Repeat the same brief with {t2} and compare the drafts side by side.
Decide who must review AI-assisted text before it is published or sent.

research.label: Research a topic with sources
workflow: Write the question you need answered and what a good answer must include.
Ask {t1} and open every cited source it gives. Note any claim without a source.
Ask the same question in {t2} and compare the sources and the conclusions.
Verify the three most important facts on the original pages before you rely on them.

meetings.label: Transcribe meetings, calls and interviews
workflow: Pick one recent recording of the kind you usually need (include real accents and background noise).
Upload it to {t1} on a free or trial plan and read the transcript against the audio for accuracy.
Run the same recording through {t2} and compare accuracy, speaker labels and export formats.
Check where recordings are stored, whether they are used for training, and who is notified when a bot joins calls.

code.label: Write, explain and review code
workflow: Choose a small, real task: a function, a bug, a test you have been avoiding.
Ask {t1} to solve it and run the result yourself; never paste secrets or private code until you have read the data policy.
Repeat with {t2} and compare correctness and explanations.
Check the plan's data-handling terms before using it on a company codebase.

images.label: Create images and graphics
workflow: Write down where the image will be used (web, print, social) and any brand rules.
Generate a few options with {t1} using the same description.
Try {t2} with the same description and compare quality, editing tools and export options.
Read the commercial-use terms before publishing anything generated.

summarize_docs.label: Summarise documents and ask questions about them
workflow: Pick one long document you actually need to understand.
Upload it to {t1} and ask for a summary, then ask three specific questions; check each answer against the document.
Try {t2} with the same document and questions.
Confirm whether uploaded files are stored and how to delete them.

general.label: A general AI assistant for many everyday tasks
workflow: List five different tasks you do in a typical week.
Try them all in {t1}; note where it helped and where you had to correct it.
Try the same tasks in {t2}.
Keep the one that handled most of your tasks, and check the plan limits you would hit in normal use.

translate.label: Transcribe and translate recordings
workflow: Choose a short recording in the language you actually work with.
Transcribe it with {t1} and have a fluent speaker check the transcript and the translation.
Repeat with {t2} and compare languages supported and accuracy.
Check which languages each plan covers before paying.

student.label: Student
student.note: Free plans carry extra weight because budgets are usually tight.

developer.label: Developer or engineer
developer.note: Code and API capabilities carry extra weight.

manager.label: Manager or team lead
manager.note: Team plans and integrations carry extra weight.

founder.label: Founder or small-business owner
founder.note: Free plans and team plans carry extra weight.

beginner.label: Beginner: I want something simple
beginner.note: No extra weight; the workflow below starts with the simplest steps.

advanced.label: Advanced: I use APIs and automation
advanced.note: API access and integrations carry extra weight.

medium.label: 11 to 50 people
medium.pilot: one small team of 3 to 5 people

large.label: More than 50 people
large.pilot: a small pilot group before any wider rollout

free_only.label: Free only: show tools with a documented free plan

flexible.label: Flexible: a free plan is nice but not required

business.label: Business budget: paid or team plans are fine

api.label: An API for my own tools
